# 0062 — Push cadence is 200 commits

- Date: 2026-08-10
- Type: feedback/governance
- Status: superseded by [0091](../../0091-push-cadence-is-300-commits.md)
- Owner: `PUSH-CADENCE-GOVERNANCE.1`

## Context

Decision `0005` retired an earlier short cadence and required explicitly
requested pushes. The director has now selected one normal push per 200 local
commits and authorized a one-time catch-up at `de9d50a5f`. That exception did
not change the standing interval.

Per-slice commits protect task recovery; batched pushes protect remote
durability without publishing every small commit.

## Decision

1. The normal automatic push cadence is one successful push after 200 local
   commits have accumulated beyond the configured upstream.
2. Derive the current count with
   `git rev-list --count @{upstream}..HEAD`. Do not store or increment a second
   mutable counter that can drift from Git.
3. Run the normal push only after the 200th slice is fully committed through
   `COMMIT.md` and the worktree is clean. Verify that a successful push leaves
   the upstream-ahead count at zero; that success begins the next interval.
4. The director may explicitly request a push before the threshold. A
   successful early push also begins a fresh interval, but the normal cadence
   remains 200 commits.
5. An unsuccessful push never resets the interval. Preserve the local commits
   and resolve or report the exact remote-state blocker before treating the
   repository as remotely durable.
6. Per-slice commit discipline is unchanged. In particular, this cadence must
   never be interpreted as permission to combine 200 slices into one commit or
   to push every individual commit.

## Consequences

- The count is exact and recoverable from Git in a fresh session.
- PNT publishes at the 200-commit boundary; an explicit early push does not
  silently shorten later intervals.
- Decision `0005` is historical rather than operative.

# 0091 — Push cadence is 300 commits

- Status: superseded by [0102](../../0102-push-cadence-is-500-commits.md)

## Context

The director increased the standing interval from 200 to 300 accumulated local commits. Per-slice commits, explicit early-push authority, and exact hosted qualification remain independent safeguards.

## Decision

1. Push normally after 300 commits beyond upstream; derive the count with `git rev-list --count @{upstream}..HEAD`, never a shadow counter.
2. Changing policy does not reset the count; only a successful push starts a new interval, so existing local commits still count.
3. A successful explicitly directed early push starts a fresh 300-commit interval without changing the standing cadence.
4. A failed or incomplete push does not reset the count; per-slice commits and mandatory hosted qualification remain unchanged.

## Consequences

- Decision `0062` becomes historical while its completed-push evidence stays exact.
- Fewer routine pushes trade a wider remote-durability interval for throughput while retaining local task-scoped crash recovery; the threshold never authorizes batched slices or skipped hosted-result consumption.

# 0108 — Decision records seal originals with stable retrieval

Date: 2026-09-27
Type: architecture / continuity
Owner: SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.51.2

## Context

The declared rationale collection reached rollover debt while a controller
architecture decision was pending. Increasing its ordinary allowance would
violate containment. The independently committed source census in
`docs/audits/decision-record-rollover-census-20260927.json` fixes record
identities and consumers before storage changes.

## Decision

Seal the complete `0001–0050` cohort in `history/0001-0050.json`. Original
UTF-8 record text is immutable and digest-checked against the prior census.
Storage does not change authority: existing supersession markers and active
policies remain exactly as written. Later semantic changes still require a
new decision and an explicit supersession reference.

Every original path remains a bounded forwarding page. The existing index
continues to discover those identities. `scripts/decision_records.py read ID`
returns original text; ordinary retrieval needs neither historical Git objects
nor network access. The generated `history/0001-0050.md` view relocates relative
links and provides stable per-record anchors. It contains no unique facts.
Its executed freshness verifier checks the entire view and all forwarding
pages against the originals, and checks affected Knowledge Map commands.

The archive is file-backed terminal storage with an exact descriptor. The
optional human view is a bounded generated projection, excluded from mandatory
bootstrap reads. Its fixed ceiling admits this sealed cohort and rendering
headers; the freshness gate prohibits appending content to either form. The
archive reader bounds every input and ID request and rejects unsafe paths,
symlinks, duplicate keys, missing/reordered records and altered original bytes.

Keep the live rationale collection's existing ceilings. Retire recovered line
and byte growth allowance; retain file-count warning pressure honestly because
stable aliases preserve cardinality. Another index/identity containment task
must precede file-count rollover. This migration grants no authority to raise
that ceiling, retire a policy, or activate the director-deferred reassessment
of other agent-era documents.

## Consequences

Direct text searches of sealed root pages now search pointers. Use the exact
reader for body searches; the affected Knowledge Map reverify commands do so.
Evidence and generated provenance retain their original decision paths.

Source identity, complete-record preservation, navigation/consumer closure,
live dimensions and residue are separate checks. Tests compare every public
reader result with the independent Git source and plant corrupt originals,
missing/duplicate/reordered members, stale views, broken aliases/index links,
missing destinations and obsolete body-search commands. Git retrieval is a
qualification oracle, not a production reader dependency.

`25c01f0127144922ade78951b91439e1d9221c08`; the tracked census is historical,

Select a finite pre-transition compatibility cohort and separate current
canonical semantic partitions. Preserve every existing root path and its
original heading destinations; freeze the compatibility population and its
rendering inputs so future records never create new root aliases. Keep the
existing sealed originals and exact reader. Place the unsealed canonical bodies

partitions. Preserve identities, authority/supersession status, all question
keys, relative destination meaning and recoverable original text. The atomic
migration must prove source identity, semantic/navigation closure, current
working-set pressure and residue separately; ceilings do not increase.

This is an actual storage/navigation change, not permission to reclassify the

membership/byte/heading proofs, and current parts remain under declared finite
bounds. `.51.3.2` must split prerequisites before moving files; `.51.3.3` proves

T1809 reads decision 0100's body/status directly; decisions 0062/0091 have

Existing exported policy/provenance path strings remain stable. The published
sealed-reader index/navigation checks need complete partition-aware closure.
Do not alter immutable audit, calibration or historical source records.

Re-derive the fixed census with the front-matter command. The producer invokes

`585070c07bbcfa1af1497ff9701924a0f9b81e01`. The transition census and original

# 0113 — ISF record interface ports reuse packed type and writer contracts

- Date: 2026-09-30
- Type: ISF language, lowering and public report contract
- Status: bounded input/output authoring admitted; complete output/consumer qualification remain open
- Owner: `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.60.4.2`

## Context

The preserved SPECFORGE request is `docs/audits/specforge-aggregate-intake-20260930/packet.json`.
Its required R1–R3 ask for declared packed record inputs/outputs, scalar field access, whole
same-type port/storage copies, and visible type/layout metadata. R4 list-root ports and R5 variant
records are optional. The intake's current refusals are historical evidence, not a new regression
oracle after delivery.

At selection, the parser admitted aggregate aliases only on storage variables. Lowering already
preserves interface type references in `+size`; core `.fsm` type/path machinery owns packed
representation. Generated internal storage handoffs do not establish authored aggregate-port
support. Decisions `0107` and `0109` retain state ownership, physical writer admission and execution
qualification. R13/R14 require stable public reports and ordered IAL1 → IAL0 lowering; this feature
must not add a second type system or bypass IAL0.

## Decision

### Source and value contract

Select `(input NAME (type T))` and `(output NAME (type T))` for an existing actor-local or imported
package-qualified alias resolving to a packed record. Reuse the existing recursive record/list
member type system, including nested members. Root list ports remain R4. Unknown types, malformed
declarations, unresolved/nonpacked types and unsupported carriers fail before successful lowering,
with the port/type/context identified. Width/type exclusivity, closed options, declaration presence
and existing domain ownership remain. Typed output reset/default options remain outside this request
and retain their current explicit refusal.

Input fields are live scalar reads in each already-supported scalar expression context: transaction
conditions, set/update RHS, rules and named drives. Existing explicit sampling remains the way to
request a snapshot. Resolve paths against the declared root type; unknown members, non-scalar leaves
and out-of-range nested items fail contextually. Do not infer fields by punctuation or admit
whole-record truthiness, arithmetic or subaggregate writes.

Whole copies involving a record port require the same resolved record type: compare recursive kind,
member names/order and scalar width/signed/state-model properties under the existing type resolver;
equal packed width alone is insufficient. Alias spelling may differ when it resolves to that same
type. Support input-to-storage and storage-to-output, then other port/storage directions whose
declared input/output roles permit the read/write. Inputs cannot become assignment targets. Preserve
existing storage-only packed transfers and scalar-port behavior; the new check applies to
record-port copies, not retroactively to all aggregate storage assignments.

Reuse typed `+size` and explicit `+interface` carrier entries. Record member order is authored
order, first member most significant, as already implemented by
`AggregatePathSupport::record_member_low_offset`. Scalar paths retain their leaf widths and exact
packed ranges. No scalarized public field pins, payload register copies, implicit reset, added
pipeline edge or silent arbitration.

### Detached public metadata

Select optional `source.interface_ports` on successful directly parsed ISF check/semantic reports,
and `interface_ports` in schedule JSON. One producer must project fresh JSON-safe values from parsed
declared ports through native, API and actual newline MCP; it must not export parser/private IR
objects. Unrelated source formats and failure reports gain no invented ISF declarations. Unknown
declaration metadata in caller-created actors remains null, rather than reconstructed from inferred
hardware signals.

The snapshot orders inputs in their authored order followed by outputs in their authored order,
matching the existing parser handoff. Entries contain `name`, `direction`, `width`, and optional
authored `type` and resolved `type_kind`; named-domain entries also contain `domain`. A record adds
`fields`, an ordered array of scalar leaves with port-relative `path`, `width`, `lsb`, `msb`,
`signed`, and optional `state_model`. Nested paths follow the existing aggregate path syntax. The
normalized semantic type catalog remains the authority for recursive type declarations. Schedule
domain details carry the same snapshot for their declared ports. Generated private handoffs do not
appear as authored top ports. Advertise every added field family in the public capability contracts
and qualify detached values and complete report parity.

### Delivery and qualification order

1. Implement the detached metadata producer on the currently admitted scalar
   interface, with record-layout producer controls. Prove unchanged scheduled
   FSM and HDL; this preparatory slice does not admit record source ports.
2. Admit and qualify packed record inputs, scalar reads and input-to-storage
   whole copies. Cover local/imported/nested types, invalid paths/types, unused
   declarations, domains and generated children under their existing bounds.
3. Admit output records and whole copies only with sound physical writer
   ownership/admission, preserving unrelated scalar and storage controls.
4. Add scalar output-field writes after qualifying physical packed-range
   overlap. Whole-root/member overlap and generated competing writers must
   refuse unless a demonstrated compatibility/exclusion contract admits them.
5. Qualify affected backend profiles and the complete supplied consumer
   outcome. Direct SystemVerilog/Verilog and supported VHDL subsets have
   separate obligations; an unsupported profile must refuse precisely.

Input delivery does not depend on general independent-controller repairs. Output writes consume
those prerequisites only where their actual behavior needs them. Native HDL observations require
existing HIAL admission and failure-only observation; never replay a spent capture to seek
recurrence. Each implementation leaf may split further before source changes.

## Consequences at selection

R1–R3 remain unshipped until their owned slices and consumer qualification pass. R4/R5 stay
separately owned optional follow-ups after required duration/timer work; transaction-local aggregate
ports, banks and variant syntax are not implicitly admitted. The book keeps present support
boundaries and labels this selection as future work. No external corpus counts, timing guarantees,
runtime signoff or downstream integration completion follow from this decision.

Permanent qualification must include independently authored packed values, member-order/type
mismatch and input-write negatives, unchanged baseline controls, complete native/API/newline
products, supported corpus cases, capability/spec/book alignment and recoverable downstream response
evidence.

## Producer implementation evidence — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.1` qualifies the detached producer independently of source admission and report
wiring. T1983 retains independently expected nested/imported ranges, signed/state-model leaves,
mutation isolation and invalid metadata. The draft's hostile controls found an argument-context
defect: a failed regex returns an empty list in list context, while an array returns its members.
Either can change the predicate/message argument slots of a validation helper. Predicates now return
explicit booleans or scalar counts; the helper also requires exact argument arity. This is a
producer repair, not a claim about uninspected validators or a public record-port implementation.

Reproduce the failed-regex mechanism independently:

```bash
perl -e 'sub predicate { $_[0] =~ /\A[01]\z/ } sub guard { print "arguments=",scalar(@_)," first=",($_[0] // "undef"),"\n" } guard(predicate(2), "error message"); guard(scalar(predicate(2)), "error message");'
```

The first call places the message in the predicate slot; the scalar call keeps both slots. The
permanent hostile controls verify refusal rather than accepting report parity as proof of valid
metadata. No native HDL runtime is established.

## Declaration report integration — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.2` captures validated parser declarations before scheduler port injection. Ordinary
module IR carries a fresh closed snapshot; domain sources select their original owned entries.
Generated transaction children have unknown declaration metadata, rather than pretending private
ports are actor declarations. Reports distinguish known empty arrays from unknown null; unrelated
and failed source reports omit the ISF source field.

The shipped preparatory surfaces are success `source.interface_ports`, schedule `interface_ports`
and owned `clock_domains[].interface_ports`, with one complete shared discovery descriptor at
`source_optional_fields.interface_ports` and `schedule_report_interface_ports`. T1984 independently
expects local/imported scalar declarations, unused/undriven entries, source order and domain
ownership; actual event crossings and generated children demonstrate private-port exclusion. This
report delivery does not admit authored records. Complete transport and supported-corpus
qualification remains explicitly owned by `.60.4.3.1.3` before record input implementation. No
native HDL runtime is claimed.

## Complete metadata qualification — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.1.3` qualifies complete typed native/API/actual newline products against independent
declaration witnesses. T1985 joins the live `build_source_query_cohort()` selector's ISF rows to
explicit reviewed source identities and declared port lists, then executes every applicable check,
semantic and schedule query. The selector owns supported catalog applicability; this is not a census
of product features, all repository fixtures or runtime coverage.
`feature.isf_declared_interface_metadata` now names this delivered metadata through the dedicated
`isf/interface_port_metadata.isf` fixture in the existing supported ISF pipeline corpus.

Local/imported aliases, unused/undriven declarations, known empty interfaces, a named empty domain,
malformed record/list/width refusals and unrelated FSM/PPIF reports receive complete transport
comparisons. Discovery compares complete native, in-process, API and newline sections. Canonical
typed JSON comparisons retain scalar kinds; shared field loss, wrong width/direction/order, private
data and stringified widths still fail independent expectations even when all three fabricated
transport copies agree. No parser or report values are repaired by the oracle. Source bytes remain
unchanged across queries.

Together with T1983/T1984 and the retained historical report/carrier/HDL controls, this closes the
preparatory declaration metadata lane. Authored record source ports and their hardware behavior
remain owned by the subsequent input/output leaves; no native HDL execution or complete consumer
delivery is established.

The corpus accounting control rejects duplicate `(relpath, classification, coverage)` tuples even
under different IDs. Reusing an existing source for the new identical contract failed that gate, so
the delivered metadata owns a separate runnable fixture. T248 also exposed stale exact expectations
from the prior storage-word-access entry (Git `3fa482924`, found with `git log -S`). The pre-slice
`241fad6b5` public catalog already exceeded those expectations; the new fixture adds only its
distinct entry. T248's exact census, tuple/ID and classification/strict checks and T1883's complete
cohort join retain the repair. Counts describe catalog entries, not independently implemented
features or runtime qualification. Recount from the live public catalog; do not reuse the old dated
qualification receipt as a current total.

## Record-input ingress selection — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.1` traces the refused input boundary before widening it. Parser
`_finalize_actor_type_references` admits aggregate aliases only on storage;
`_validate_actor_aggregate_storage_paths`, rule operand maps and enum disambiguation currently
select storage roots. Adding inputs to one map is insufficient. Use a shared declaration-root
description, with transaction locals/formals and drive parameters masking outer names in their
actual scope. An input shadowed by a writable formal must not become that formal's role; an
unresolved local must not borrow its outer type or placeholder width. The existing formal resolver
and domain ownership remain authoritative.

Prepare a strict resolved-record identity gate separately from
`PayloadTypeSupport::payload_compatible_with_type_spec`. That public helper intentionally checks
payload shape and scalar width, allowing different signed and state-model facts. Preserve it for its
existing callers. Port copies compare recursive kinds, ordered record members, ordered list
children, widths, signed values and optional resolved state-model presence/value. Unspecified stays
unspecified; do not substitute a backend rendering default. Alias names are not part of resolved
identity. Malformed/unresolved roots fail contextually.

Transaction conditions, switch values, set/update RHS, rule guards/assignments, named-drive
bodies/actuals and inline drives need explicit scalar-versus-copy checks from the first admission.
Whole-record values are permitted only in qualified same-type assignments with allowed declaration
roles; expression operators, truthiness and subaggregate writes refuse. Existing storage-only packed
transfers retain their separate contract. Domain lookup resolves a path to its declared root,
honoring lexical masking and preserving the authored path in diagnostics; it must not invent a
crossing from a same-named formal.

The current aggregate validator handles `set`, but not `update` or `sample` leaf paths. Sampling
width collection copies exact root widths, not resolved leaf facts. Input delivery therefore owns
explicit scalar-leaf sampling in entry/body contexts, with resolved width/type and existing capture
timing. Whole-record sampling into an inferred alias remains outside this bounded delivery. No
hidden sample, delayed edge or new aggregate local is introduced. Typed `+size` and explicit
`+interface` already preserve unused declarations; generated/domain routes must retain those
identities before behavior signoff.

Reproduce the historical identity/refusal control at pre-admission revision
`0d01ca3fc8f880acf926ae59305843a1172bf1d3`, without HDL:

```bash
scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- perl -Iperl -MFSM::Adapter::ISF -MFSM::Package::PayloadTypeSupport -MJSON::PP -e '
my $p = FSM::Adapter::ISF->new;
my $a = $p->parse_source(q{(actor controls
  (types (type plain (record (payload (bits 8)))) (type alias plain)
    (type signed_frame (record (payload (signed (bits 8)))))
    (type four (record (payload (four_state (bits 8)))))
    (type two (record (payload (two_state (bits 8))))))
  (interface (output done))
  (storage (var a (type plain)) (var b (type alias))
    (var c (type signed_frame)) (var d (type four)) (var e (type two)))
  (transaction main (complete done)))}, "controls.isf");
my @t = map { $_->{type_spec} } @{$a->{storage}};
my $j = JSON::PP->new->canonical;
die "alias mismatch" unless $j->encode($t[0]) eq $j->encode($t[1]);
for my $pair ([0,2], [0,3], [3,4]) {
  die "control lost" unless $j->encode($t[$pair->[0]]) ne $j->encode($t[$pair->[1]])
    && FSM::Package::PayloadTypeSupport->payload_compatible_with_type_spec(@t[@$pair]);
}
my $ok = eval { $p->parse_source(q{(actor refused
  (types (type frame (record (payload (bits 8)))))
  (interface (input packet (type frame)) (output done))
  (storage (var held (type frame)))
  (transaction main (set held packet) (complete done)))}, "refused.isf"); 1 };
die "refusal lost: $@" if $ok || $@ !~ /interface port.*references aggregate type/;
print "alias identity, distinct property controls and input refusal verified\n";
'
```

The input lane now separately owns closed gates, source admission, generated/ domain carriers and
independent HDL/public completion. This planning receipt does not establish new input acceptance,
sampling support or native behavior.

## Unwired value-gate qualification — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.2` prepares `ISFRecordPortValues` without parser or scheduler wiring.
`record_value_scope` takes closed resolved outer/local declarations; the nearest binding masks its
outer type and role even when unresolved. `record_value_reference` retains scalar path
type/width/range through `AggregatePathSupport`, refuses input writes and whole/subaggregate scalar
values, and returns unknown tokens to their existing validator. The caller must still validate those
tokens and supply actual lexical bindings; a prepared map does not establish parser, domain or
generated-child integration.

`validate_record_port_copy` uses the existing composition declared-type comparison after closed
resolved-shape validation by the qualified declaration producer. Root aliases are absent from that
identity. Equal packed widths, renamed/reordered members, bit/bits kinds, nested shape/list order,
signed and optional state-model differences are independently distinguished. Transfers with no whole
record port keep their existing scalar/storage assignment owner. Scalar formal/local slices use a
one-member wrapper for existing core traversal; the wrapper preserves offsets and adds no source
carrier or type declaration.

T1986's draft negative helper matched an expected regex passed as a caller argument inside
`Carp::confess` stack text. That concealed a wrong-key diagnostic projection (`reason` instead of
the resolver's `code`), yielding `unresolved` for otherwise specific invalid paths. Restricting the
oracle to the first diagnostic line first made the unknown-member/index/syntax controls fail. The
producer now retains the core code. A permanent independently wrong message with the expected
pattern only in its stack demonstrates the original false match and the corrected oracle's
rejection. This is a repaired unshipped draft and test-helper defect, not a finding about
uninspected diagnostic oracles.

T1986 retains resolved alias/imported positives, independently authored ranges, same-width
counterexamples, lexical unresolved/scalar/formal shadows, input-role negatives, malformed/cyclic
facts, storage-only bypass and unchanged aggregate source refusal. T1983/T1259 and core path,
structural type and interface-boundary controls pass alongside it. Source admission, sample timing,
carriers, complete public products and HDL behavior remain owned by later leaves.

## Contextual integration and domain prerequisite — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.1` splits actual lexical/contextual gate preparation, explicit leaf sampling
carriers, declared-domain protection, first input admission and frontend/public replay before
implementation. Parser type finalization precedes aggregate/enum checks, but their current maps
select storage roots. Locals, formals, drive parameters and explicit samples require their actual
binding facts; inferred writes must not redefine an actor input. Sampling preparation must retain
signed/state facts as well as leaf width through existing typed carriers, with no new snapshot edge
or whole-record inferred local.

At pre-repair revision `02827d840254d6cdbfa4020be7910bb7ae9ac4cb`, public parse/lower probes reject
a foreign-domain whole scalar input and unsliced record-storage member, yet accept the same input's
bit/indexed slices and the member/storage scalar slices. `_validate_domain_signal_access` recognizes
only single-index path suffixes and only actor-storage roots for non-identifiers. The missing colon
form and interface-root exclusion bypass domain admission. This proves a source/lowering validation
defect; no HDL runtime is established. P1 repair `.60.4.3.2.3.4.1` is next, before unrelated
contextual implementation; `.4.2` retains future record/formal/domain qualification. Do not widen
the matcher blindly into enum/package namespaces or erase nearest-binding roles.

Reproduce the bounded existing source defect without native HDL execution:

```bash
scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- perl -Iperl -MFSM::Adapter::ISF -MFSM::Scheduler::ISF -MJSON::PP -e '
my $header = q{(actor domain_probe
 (clock-domains (domain core (clock clk) :default) (domain aux (clock aux_clk)))
 (types (type frame (record (payload (bits 8)))))
 (interface (input start) (input data (width 8) (domain aux)) (output seen (width 8)))
 (storage (var record_value (type frame) (domain aux)) (var scalar (width 8) (domain aux)))};
my @rows;
for my $token (qw(record_value.payload record_value.payload[3:0] scalar[3:0] data data[3:0] data[0])) {
 my $ok = eval {
  my $a = FSM::Adapter::ISF->new->parse_source($header
    . "(transaction main (on start) (set seen $token)))", "domain-probe.isf");
  FSM::Scheduler::ISF->new->lower($a); 1;
 };
 my ($message) = split /\n/, $@;
 push @rows, {token => $token, accepted => $ok ? JSON::PP::true : JSON::PP::false,
   diagnostic => $message // ""};
}
print JSON::PP->new->canonical->pretty->encode(\@rows);
'
```

Before repair, `record_value.payload` and `data` refuse with their authored foreign-domain
ownership; the slice/index cases accept. Permanent first-line negative oracles and
same-domain/lexical/enum/package/crossing controls must retain the repair. After repair this dated
receipt remains historical; the current command and owning task establish present admission.

## Existing domain-path repair — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.4.1` closes the confirmed existing source-validation defect before record
admission. Domain lookup now recognizes scalar colon slices and uses the nearest declared
actor/formal/local root for indexed references. Dotted paths retain their existing storage
classification, preserving enum and package names. Future authored record-input member ownership
remains under `.4.2`, after scoped contextual preparation; record source ports still refuse.

T1920 first goes RED on the recorded foreign member/storage slices and input slice/index controls,
then passes the repair. Its first diagnostic line must name the exact path, access and declared
domains. Nested list/member slices, reversed and single-bit ranges, same-domain values, unrelated
enum names and explicit generated formal shadows are included. The unchanged command above now
rejects every recorded foreign case with its authored ownership message.

T1985 adds complete typed native/API/actual newline check/semantic comparisons and existing schedule
transport errors for these sources, with independent exact diagnostic messages, absent successful
declaration snapshots, no partial schedule and unchanged source bytes. T1982 preserves complete
earlier domain reports, actual scheduled FSM files and SystemVerilog/Verilog HDL except date.
T1247/T1259/T1986 retain domain partition, storage/types and unwired value gates. This repairs
validation; it establishes no new record authoring, general controller repair, native HDL runtime or
downstream completion.

## Actual declaration-scope preparation — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.2.1` prepares detached actor, transaction and drive scopes in
`ISFRecordPortScopes`. Actor ports and `var` storage consume finalized declaration widths and
resolved type facts. Transaction formals replace outer declarations; explicit top-level local
clauses provide the nearest width-only binding. Resolved type facts retain signed and optional
state-model properties. An unresolved typed declaration never uses its placeholder width. Symbolic
local widths remain unknown because existing local admission requires positive literal widths; that
admission is not changed by this projection.

Named-drive parameters carry names without resolved types. They mask outer roles and types without
inferring a type from a drive target. Assignment targets create no declarations here. Explicit
sample aliases and their leaf facts remain owned by `.3.3`; contextual AST and enum/rule namespace
integration remain under `.3.2.2` and `.3.2.3`. These helpers are unwired, and record authoring
still refuses.

T1987 independently expects parsed symbolic/scalar/formal facts and imported record identity, exact
packed leaf ranges, signed/state properties, unresolved shadows, known input roles and mutation
isolation. Malformed declared widths, duplicate port roles and invalid parameter names fail.
Complete parsed actors and scheduled objects, including emitted file bytes, remain unchanged after
projection. The first draft fixture incorrectly assumed an authored pin/storage collision was
accepted; the actual parser refused it. The corrected fixture retains that refusal and the existing
explicit-local pin-collision refusal. Caller-supplied conflicting facts cannot erase a pin role, but
their projection establishes no new source admission or physical identity contract.

Reverify with guarded T1987/T1986/T1983/T1259/T1391. The competing borrowed-type, placeholder-width
and inferred-target interpretations fail the independent scope/range witnesses and negative
controls. Tracked producers, source controls and tests make this preparation reproducible; no sample
timing, new public transport field, generated-child carrier or native HDL behavior is established.

Contextual preparation and first-touch caller-data correction are retained in
[0114](../../0114-record-value-validation-detaches-facts-before-reading.md). The original scope mutation
baseline followed an earlier projection; fresh copied facts now have independent pre-projection
controls. This qualification remains unwired.

Current record/formal domain preparation, repaired inline/named-drive ingress and the owned
unused-drive carrier defect are canonical in
[0114](../../0114-record-value-validation-detaches-facts-before-reading.md#recordformal-path-domain-preparation--2026-09-30).
The earlier domain receipts above retain their original capture boundaries.

## Parser/module gate integration — 2026-09-30

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.5.1` integrates prepared validation before `.5.2` admits record-input source
syntax. Parser resolved-type phases and shared formal/ executable module preparation now apply the
contextual scalar/copy/role/sample gate whenever actual record-input facts exist. Existing
storage-only path grammar remains with its original validator. Record-bearing enum exclusions use

# 0114 — Record value validation detaches facts before reading

- Date: 2026-09-30
- Status: qualified context/sample/domain preparation; authored input admission follows 0113
- Owner: `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.60.4.3.2.3.2.2`
- Parent contract: [0113](../../0113-isf-record-interface-ports-reuse-packed-type-and-writer-contracts.md)

## Context

Record inputs need contextual scalar reads and strict same-type copies before
their first authored source admission. Existing qualified value gates accept
resolved declaration facts, and detached scope preparation consumes parsed
actor/formal/local declarations and untyped drive parameters. This preparation
is still unwired; current scalar/storage authoring remains unchanged.

T1988's complete actor comparison exposed a mutation missed by the earlier
T1987 baseline: validation changed string widths into JSON numbers on fresh
copies of parsed facts. The earlier mutation baseline followed a previous
projection. Direct fresh parser controls stayed equal; the fresh copied
controls were RED. T1986 independently reproduced the same change in each
scope, reference and copy gate using explicitly string-valued widths.

## Decision

Detach caller-owned declaration/type/reference maps before numeric validation
or comparison. Perl numeric reads can change a scalar's flags and subsequent
JSON representation without an assignment to that scalar. A clone made after
validation cannot protect the original. `Storable::dclone` detaches before
reads and retains cycles for the existing closed type validator to reject;
core type/path/layout contracts remain unchanged.

Reproduce the mechanism independently:

```bash
perl -MJSON::PP -e 'my $j=JSON::PP->new->canonical; my $x={width=>"7"}; print $j->encode($x),"\n"; my $n=0+$x->{width}; print $j->encode($x),"\n";'
```

The outputs are `{"width":"7"}` then `{"width":7}`. This is a caller-data
mutation mechanism, not a new numeric value or public field contract.

`ISFRecordPortContexts` now prepares selected transaction set/update RHS,
when/while/until conditions, switch selectors/branches, nested bodies, rule
guards/assignments, named/inline drive bodies and named-drive actuals. Whole
record ports refuse scalar contexts, including negated and compact comparison
spellings. Port-involved whole assignments consume qualified recursive type
identity and role gates; input targets, bad paths, operator-position paths and
unsupported subaggregate uses refuse. Existing storage-only packed transfers
retain their original owner. Explicit leaf sampling, domain ownership and
first source admission remain separate prerequisites.

The gate validates references, not the complete source grammar. Unknown tokens,
operator/arity/static-value rules and enum/package member validation retain
their existing validators. State-active arguments denote states, and local/
parameter declaration names are not read operands. No successful preparatory
gate establishes that an otherwise invalid source is accepted.

A scalar pin may share an enum/package root name. Actual namespace roots remain
delegated unless the nearest aggregate or an explicitly shadowed outer
aggregate identifies a declaration path. The draft incorrectly rejected the
admitted enum token `mode.BUSY` when the actor had scalar input `mode`.
T1988 retains the repaired source control and the counterexample in which a
scalar formal must not borrow a same-named outer record's member via an enum.
Common aggregate/enum/rule root projection is prepared below; frontend integration remains pending.

## Qualification and limits

T1987's fresh copied actor/transaction/drive controls first reproduce the scalar
kind change; T1986's independently authored typed JSON does so for each value
gate. All preserve complete caller products after the repair. T1988 retains
independent selected AST cases and exact first-line negatives, same-type alias
copies, equal-width signed/state mismatches, input writes, formal shadows,
unknown-path controls, unsupported sampling/count/trigger contexts and enum
delegation. Complete currently admitted parser and scheduled products, including
emitted file bytes, remain unchanged. No oracle normalizes the caller product
before comparison.

```bash
scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh -- prove -Iperl \
  t/1988-isf-record-port-context-gates.t \
  t/1987-isf-record-port-declaration-scopes.t \
  t/1986-isf-record-port-value-gates.t \
  t/1983-isf-interface-port-metadata.t \
  t/1259-isf-aggregate-storage-type-aliases.t t/1391-isf-local-variables.t
```

The competing borrowed-type, whole-record scalar, equal-width identity and
post-read detachment interpretations fail independent witnesses and negative
controls. Producers and permanent source/AST controls are tracked; ignored
logs are supplementary. This establishes unwired preparation and the repaired
caller-data contract, not new source/public transport admission, sample timing,
generated/domain carriers, external HDL execution or complete consumer delivery.

## Common root-classification preparation

roots and actor rule-declaration roots. Transaction locals/formals and drive
parameters never become actor rule inputs. Rule roots also retain authored

Nearest scalar or unresolved bindings remove an outer record from aggregate
traversal while keeping that outer name excluded from enum fallback. Scalar
pins that only share an enum/package root remain namespace tokens. Member
validity and enum/package resolution stay with their existing owners; root
classification does not turn an unknown member into a valid value.

The unwired contextual gate consumes this common projection instead of its
private namespace classifier. Existing frontend aggregate/enum/rule validators
remain unchanged until sampling/domain prerequisites permit source integration.
This is deliberate preparation, not record authoring or carrier admission.
T1989 independently expects every map and tests actual imported enum/type/

declaration collisions for private record-derived aliases and inconsistent

type may reuse their own alias. A record-derived alias cannot replace authored

A separate pure type-product boundary generates ordinary core scalar type ASTs,
type references and exact widths only for record-derived aliases. Private type
names are sorted and deterministically reserve existing names before suffixing
collisions. Signed and declared two/four-state wrappers are retained; no backend
state default, reset/default fact or hardware edge is introduced. The actual
public type resolver reconstructs these scalar properties independently.

Module widths/types, actual generated-helper/private alias ownership and full

## Selector shape validation precedes dereference

The `.3.3.2.1` draft selector read `type_spec` from an unchecked input entry.
A direct first-touch call returned false but changed caller `inputs` from
`[null]` to `[{}]`: Perl autovivified the undefined array entry. T1991's added
malformed-entry controls went RED for the mutation and unclassified raw hash
errors. This is distinct from the earlier numeric-flag mutation mechanism.

Reproduce autovivification independently:

```bash
perl -MJSON::PP -e 'my $j=JSON::PP->new->canonical; my $a=[undef]; print $j->encode($a),"\n"; my $unused=$a->[0]{type_spec}; print $j->encode($a),"\n";'
```

The outputs are `[null]` then `[{}]`. The repair validates interface/input-list
shape and each declaration map before its first dereference. It scans the full
list so a valid record prefix cannot conceal a malformed suffix. Absent
interfaces remain absent. Permanent first-touch controls preserve complete
caller JSON on both successful and refused selection; existing sample and
context controls remain qualified. At selector qualification, no public parser
or module emitter consumed it. Module preparation now follows below.

checks its targets and expressions in its actual activation-site domain. Its
scalar parameter names mask outer declarations with that domain. Unused bodies
have no activation owner and are not checked by this new call-site gate.
Nearest parameter shadows, nested record input body reads, same-domain paths
and explicit crossing contracts pass. T1985 adds complete native/API/newline
check and semantic diagnostic parity, existing schedule transport refusal,
no successful declaration/partial schedule products and unchanged source bytes
for admitted inline/named foreign read/write sources.

messages, nearest bindings and foreign scalar namespace witnesses; durability

constant with a false aux-to-core clock-domain violation. The production
condition passes the complete enum and imported-package controls. Marking
every scalar input as a record root is therefore not a valid domain repair.

## Owned unused-drive domain carrier defect

SEM `.60.4.3.2.3.4.3` repairs the separate P2 strict-replay defect before
authored record input admission. This ordinary admitted scalar source
reproduces it without record-port preparation:

```lisp
(actor unused_drive_domains
 (clock-domains (domain core (clock clk) :default) (domain aux (clock aux_clk)))
 (interface (input start) (input data (width 8)) (output seen (width 8)) (output done))
 (drive (publish value) (seen value))
 (transaction main (on start) (set seen data) (complete done)))
```

Save it under a repository-local path and run native
`./bin/fsmgen --quiet --strict --check --json PATH`. At the predecessor above,
success is false and no generated output is emitted. The diagnostic names
undeclared top input `publish_value`: core's child input has width 8 while
aux's has width 1, blocking consistent inference. The drive is unused. The
same cause breaks positive prepared top replay, independently of record types.
At pre-repair `68880895fc4635f04b631f705ad548a600bddb3f`, DomainSource
copies every drive definition into every local actor. `_build_drive_dts`
creates request/payload helpers for those bodies; `_drive_param_width` infers
width from local outputs, defaulting to one where the foreign target is absent.
The top then sees incompatible invented inputs. The private partition now
retains sorted drive names from its existing validated activation-site map,
including generated transactions. The shared actual/formal domain constructor
clones only those definitions. Missing, malformed, unknown or duplicate
selections refuse; selected body mutations cannot reach caller declarations.
Public domain projections keep their existing closed fields.

Re-derive with guarded T1996 and the owning leaf's focused cohort. Its literal
per-domain definition sets, absent inactive request/payload names and strict
replay of every actual domain/top/generated carrier distinguish selection
from mere transport parity. Complete native/API/actual newline check, semantic
and schedule products agree, with unchanged source bytes and caller JSON.
Nested calls in distinct domains and generated-child calls retain used bodies.
The exact ordinary source above now reports strict success.

Falsification includes the captured complete pre-repair T1996 RED controls.
An isolated repository-local DomainSource copy replacing only
`$domain_actor{drives} = \%drives;` with `$domain_actor{drives} = {};` makes the
used nested case terminate with `Transaction 'main': drive 'publish' not defined`
at LoweringIR.pm:8838. Dropping all definitions is therefore not a valid repair.
Durability is T1996, the two tracked producers, the immutable predecessor and
this exact source/control recipe; ignored logs are supplemental. The initial
transport fixture mistakenly used the qualified-corpus row helper for dynamic
source IDs. Corrected tests use the existing actual capture protocol; no public

# 0103 — Public regression-promotion policy loads a tracked seal

- Date: 2026-09-23
- Type: verification architecture / regression promotion
- Status: accepted
- Refines: [0096](../../0096-regression-promotion-uses-a-current-eleven-profile-corpus.md)
- Implementation owner: `HOSTED-VIAL-REGRESSION-GATE-RESULT.2`

## Context

Decision 0096 made `FSM::VIAL::ArchitectureScaleRegressionPromotionPolicy` the
caller-sealed executable authority and required public derivation to
authenticate the immutable v1 closure before recomputing the eleven-profile
selection. That closure lives under ignored
`.artifacts/qualification/vial-scale/v1/calibration-closure-v1`. The first
hosted `vial-gate` command failed there, before any profile result, because a
fresh checkout does not carry the publication.

The policy object that derivation emits is already pinned. Qualification and
the tracked corpus bind
`regression-promotion-policy/19cf41056da86d95c266597e7db76eff3810ee29511a005e1051053009a65ece`.
Local derivation from the historical closure produces that same identity. The
current corpus and qualification already travel as a tracked evidence bundle.
The ignored closure does not, and committing it would republish historical
measurement bytes the public gate does not execute.

## Decision

1. Public `derive` loads one tracked canonical document at
   `vial/qualification/regression_promotion_policy/regression-promotion-policy-v1.json`.
   It requires the repository RAM guard, a regular same-volume file, canonical
   JSON, the existing policy validator, the pinned identity above, historical
   disposition, and current-performance ineligibility. Caller-injected evidence
   remains rejected.
2. The tracked document is the already-derived policy object. Its identity does
   not change. It is not the ignored closure publication and it is not a new
   measurement.
3. `_derive_from_report` remains the historical comparison used by local
   mutation tests when the ignored closure is present. Public derivation, the
   capture plan, and the gate contract do not call it and do not require that
   publication.
4. A failed or unavailable hosted run remains neither support nor capacity.
   This decision does not rewrite the local exact-pinned observation and does
   not invent a hosted pass. A fresh checkout can load the sealed policy; a
   hosted result still requires a hosted run.

## Consequences

- Decision 0096 item 9 and its re-derive leg described runtime authentication
  of the v1 publication. That runtime requirement is refined here. The
  eleven-profile selection, historical comparison figures, provider rule, and
  nonclaims in 0096 stay in force.
- The public gate can pass policy derivation on a checkout that has the tracked
  seal and the existing tracked corpus and qualification evidence.
- Historical closure mutation tests remain local-only. They are not the public
  command.

## Rollback

Remove the tracked seal, restore public derivation to the ignored publication,
and return `HOSTED-VIAL-REGRESSION-GATE-RESULT.2` to active. Do not treat that
rollback as a hosted result.

Before `IAL2-FEATURE-COMPLETENESS-FRONTIER.794`, the byte-lane HBURST `SEQ`

body and nonzero counts preserve the sampled delay.

and paired BUSY-composition sources. Generic ISF dynamic-wait lowering and APB
wait generation were not changed by `.794`.

`BACKEND-LANGUAGE-PORTABILITY-CONTRACT-FRONTIER.2.3` completed a candidate
portable in-memory request/result API family, not a Perl module API name. The
conceptual entrypoints are `capabilities(request?)` and `execute(request)`,
with operation tokens for `check`, `lower`, `schedule`, `semantic`,
`generate_hdl`, and `verification_output`.

The candidate API is source-text and source-identity based. It must not
require POSIX filesystem paths, process spawning, Perl module loading, Perl
object receivers, raw private AST/IR objects, or raw HDLGenerator result
hashes in the pure in-memory path.

Generated review, HDL, and verification artifacts should return as JSON-safe
virtual artifact entries with stable relative identities, kind, role,
language, content, source layer, and generated-from provenance. The filesystem
CLI remains an adapter over that model.

The original focused `t/301` resource cliff on
`ppif/axi_manager_capacity_status_dynamic_write_depth3_same_id_issue_order_queue.ppif`
was recovered by `.2.3.1` with a bounded oversized PPIF check-json summary
path. A full guarded `t/301` rerun remains host-memory-policy blocked in the
current environment. `.2.4` has since selected the source-catalog plus
artifact-sink host abstraction, `.2.5` selected the Perl-reference parity
harness and normalization rules, `.2.6` selected the mdBook
implementation-blueprint chapter structure, and the next active selector is
`.2.7`.

`BACKEND-LANGUAGE-PORTABILITY-CONTRACT-FRONTIER.2.5` selected a differential
parity harness model with the current Perl 5 implementation as the
reference/oracle. Future implementation-language variants must run the same
logical `.2.3` request family over the same `.2.4` source graph, normalize
host-specific details, and compare the normalized public result against the
Perl oracle before claiming feature support.

The selected corpus partitions are `supported_smoke`, `strict_supported`,
`expected_failure`, `legacy_out_of_scope`, and `resource_sensitive`. Public
parity covers capability manifests, check JSON, semantic JSON, lowering and
schedule artifacts, generated HDL behavior, shipped verification outputs,
diagnostics, support accounting, and semantic-introspection/MCP surfaces for
variants that claim them.

Normalization removes host-specific paths, temp directories, output roots, JSON
key ordering, line endings, and resource measurements while preserving public
source identity, support accounting, diagnostics, artifact identities, and HDL
semantics. Broad `t/301`/`t/303` style gates remain logical parity targets, but
resource-sensitive runs must use `scripts/run_with_ram_guard.sh` or exact
bounded replacement tests. `.2.6` has since selected the mdBook
implementation-blueprint chapter structure, and the next active
backend-portability selector is `.2.7`, typed extension/plugin portability.

`BACKEND-LANGUAGE-PORTABILITY-CONTRACT-FRONTIER.2.7` selected the typed
extension portability boundary. The current extension system remains a bounded
Perl reference implementation surface, but it is not a backend-language-neutral
portable plugin API.

Perl-specific mechanics include blessed extension objects, `Module::Name`
loading through `@INC`/`require`, real `new()` constructor discovery,
`UNIVERSAL::can`, `FSM::Extension::*` object receiver shapes, live Perl
pipeline/result objects, and direct mutation of raw in-process result hashes.

Typed extension/plugin support is out of scope for the first non-Perl
implementation experiment unless a future exact task selects a portable
extension API first. A non-Perl variant that does not implement that future API
must advertise extension support as unsupported and fail closed on extension
loading requests. `.2.8` selected the same-repository Rust/Rust-Wasm portable
API smoke experiment. The `.3.1` through `.3.3` slices then scaffolded the Rust
contract crate, added one direct `.fsm` check smoke, and proved that result
against the Perl oracle.

`CI-PERL-FSM-REGRESSION-JUN15-REPAIR.1` repaired GitHub run `27531373582`.
HDLGenerator had rejected supported `.isf` and `.ppif` roots under a
`.fsm`-only guard; tests also had three stale contracts recorded in the task.
The repaired facade accepts scalar, exact-one-argument `.fsm`, `.isf`, and
`.ppif` roots. Local `./bin/ci-regression` passed (`Files=1437`, `Tests=11200`)
with its trailing mdBook build.

For PPIF, the in-memory facade compiles one generated `.fsm` entry artifact
and reports it as `source_info.generated_hdl_entry_artifact`; the CLI can emit
the aggregate top. The registry therefore keeps `expected_module_name` as the
shared/CLI oracle and declares `expected_pipeline_module_name` for the 62 of
240 strict entries whose pipeline module differs: 18 AHB, 37 APB, five AXI
composition, and two valid-ready bundles. `t/296` checks the pipeline module
and exact entry artifact independently; the bundles explicitly override the
artifact expectation because wrapper filenames and emitted monitor modules
differ. CLI assertions retain the aggregate-module oracle.

The default/strict pipeline/CLI cohorts use deterministic self-workers—one
pipeline entry or four CLI entries—so allocator and file-cache growth is
released below the unchanged 4096-MiB descendant-RSS cap. The facade remains
limited to `.fsm`, `.isf`, and `.ppif`; 86 supported profile aliases (28
`.ahb`, 57 `.apb`, one `.axi`) remain CLI-only, are excluded from both pipeline
cohorts, and remain checked in both CLI cohorts.

GitHub `Perl FSM Regression` run `27621526955` failed on commit `8c39827f`
because `t/1436-ial2-ppif-parser-cli.t` contained PPIF CLI `--verify-hdl`
subtests that expected Verilator and Yosys to be installed on the hosted
runner. The CLI correctly reported `Missing external HDL validation tool(s):
verilator, yosys`; the test policy was stale.

`CI-PPIF-VERIFY-HDL-TOOL-DEPENDENCY-REPAIR.1` aligns those PPIF tests with the
existing optional external-validation policy already used by
`t/308-systemverilog-external-validation.t`: PPIF `--verify-hdl` checks are
skipped when required external tools are unavailable, while non-HDL PPIF
coverage continues to run.

The same `t/1436` file passes in a simulated no-tool environment
(`PATH=/usr/bin:/bin`) and in the normal tool-equipped local environment, so
the guard does not suppress Verilator/Yosys coverage when the tools exist.

Every current inventory candidate path belongs to exactly one bounded migration
group. Each recorded outcome joins a stable current candidate ID to one of four
forms: a published claim record on the same source path, a non-aliased
three-leg derived gate, a reviewed-incidental reason, or a task-owned evidence
gap. A group becomes required-complete only when its migration slice closes;
the checker then rejects any remaining open candidate. The join detects stale
or duplicate candidate IDs, but it does not turn the reviewer's classification
or declared evidence into semantic truth.

The foundational root review also demonstrates the repair rule. An exact
experimental UVM peak had no tracked measurement producer, while the selected
guarded-envelope outcome and lower-memory compilation control were preserved by
the checked probe. The unsupported point estimate was removed instead of being
reclassified as evidence. Immutable book-partition and roadmap-occupancy
measurements remain historical dispositions whose reasons name their Git
producer, preserved independent audit, and durability path; live ledger,
complete-roadmap-archive, and provider-source-order claims use derived gates.

The bridge/execution review keeps each selected scale axis attached to its own
producer and separating oracle. Source-map calibration is differentially
rebuilt from baseline and one-record semantic shapes before the exact boundary
suite runs. Scenario-map collision is retained as pre-repair history with a
current uniqueness watcher. Total and live fibers use different generated tree
shapes, while execution types require real bound endpoints; rejected wide-tree
and unbound-alias examples are reviewed context rather than claim evidence.

The final root review keeps the checking families separate as well. The
foundation oracle derives owned and rejected catalog shapes. The model oracle
counts authored definitions, instances, declarations, and exercised cells;
scoreboard, coverage, and fault oracles independently reconstruct storage,
order, and lifecycle identities with targeted mutations. The random-replay
oracle distinguishes semantic preflight, bridge materialization, plan
rejection, and the adjacent semantic diagnostic. Exact guarded runs close the
root group, whose registry is now required-complete.

The first general-book review keeps compact language examples from becoming
accidental measurements. Grammar rejections, inferred widths, literal
normalization, declarative state models, composition inference, expression
factorization, hosted-test partitioning, target-language emission, and repeat
lowering use their ordinary tracked producers and focused behavior oracles.
Syntax operands, boolean option values, protocol-version tokens, test bands,
and linked test filenames are reviewed as non-claims. The LTE expected-failure
count has an additional source-derived control that counts the active child
entries independently of the catalog's diagnostic pattern.

The intent/actor/transaction review closes 42 behavior candidates with exact
derived gates and keeps the literal value in `(set fire 1)` as a reviewed
example numeral. It repaired two overstated book claims: positive static
repeat is check-first and costs `N × (body + 1) + 2`, while drive-parameter
payload width follows the driven target and only a scalar payload is one bit.
The focused timing oracle proves those distinctions across entry, drive,
sample, await, complete, control, data, loop, and latency forms. Lowering also
stamps every state with its exact transaction owner so injected latency states
remain reportable; the JSON emitter uses that field first and fails closed
when no legacy owner can be derived.

The control/data/composition/lowering review closes 60 behavior candidates
through distinct loop, temporal, control, width, storage, composition, rule,
timing, and type evidence families. Generated-child route claims run through
the exhaustive scalar/vector, ingress/egress, multi-route, report, generated-
top, HDL, and RED matrix rather than sharing a copied width assertion. Seven
numbered verification-example headings and the runnable clamp threshold are
reviewed instructional/example values. The lowering reference now repeats the
correct check-first timing and distinguishes request width, per-formal signal
count, and target-derived payload width; both remain explicit inventory claims
rather than disappearing through prose reformatting.

The support-matrix/non-protocol-backlog review closes 62 behavior candidates
through distinct support, book-audit, SourceHIR, VHDL-generic, ATL/FIFO, IAL2,
and VIAL evidence families. Nine test, recipe, task, language-generation, and
syntax-example numerals remain reviewed identifiers or example values rather
than capability measurements. The executable book audit reports 82 complete
fixtures lowering cleanly, so the stale hand-copied total in Chapter 14 is
repaired and remains watched by that audit.

The blueprint/platform/reference review closes 14 current behavior or recovery
claims through Rust parity, AHB truth, retired-history, ledger, task-tree,
evidence-map, ISF-partition, and roadmap gates. Thirty-seven chapter
coordinates, policy inputs, old-guide section labels, and immutable activation
measurements remain reviewed context. Activation-only occupancy is written in
the past tense so it cannot be mistaken for current repository state. With all
five general-book children closed, the group is required-complete at its exact
inventory boundary and any reopened or stale identity fails the disposition
checker.

The first protocol review separates executable AXI manager surfaces from the
chronology that led to them. Twenty-eight current queue-depth, slot, rule,
assertion, completion-demux, runtime-validation, and output-bank claims derive
from the ordinary AXI capacity/status builder and bounded public PPIF fixtures;
focused generator and dynamic-ID oracles distinguish head ordering, RLAST
qualification, group-local depth, matched-beat capture, and per-transaction
lane ownership. Thirty-seven selector boundaries, temporary helper counts,
host-memory percentages, stopped-probe byte counts, and superseded local gates
remain reviewed history whose reasons name their exact durable audit or
selection record. They do not become current capability or resource promises.

The foundational APB review closes six current completer, multi-register,
data16, sideband, and queued-timing candidates through the ordinary requester,
completer, and composition producers. Focused endpoint and composition oracles
separate source order, address alignment, mapped access, byte-lane masking,
end-to-end widths, one-entry queueing, overflow rejection, and generated
review artifacts. Five status-width, multi-register, and sideband numerals
remain reviewed inputs from their exact contract-selection records rather than
being double-counted as independent runtime measurements.

The next APB review closes 13 current data16, remaining-width, protection,
queued-timing, queued-sideband, and two-peripheral propagation statements
through the ordinary requester, completer, composition, alias, endpoint, and
interconnect gates. Twenty-two pre-data16 guard values, selected width/status/
queue contracts, readiness scopes, and superseded 32-bit-only timing guards
remain reviewed chronology. Their exact selection commits stay durable, while
the later behavior has its own generated-artifact and negative-boundary proof.

The multi-register/protection/composition review closes 17 current behavior
candidates through nine family-specific gates. Fixed and multi-peripheral,
16-bit and 32-bit, no-policy and protected, and status/control versus
`reg0`/`reg1` shapes retain distinct public fixtures and falsification paths.
Twenty-nine readiness, selector, and contract numerals remain reviewed
chronology tied to their exact `.619` through `.652` Git records. The current
behavior gates independently prove queueing, adjacent setup, register and
window decode, byte masks, protection ownership, report residue, artifacts,
and profile-alias parity.

The generalized register-set review closes 14 current behavior candidates
through six distinct 16/32-bit, no-policy/protected, two-to-four-register, and

Ordinary ISF generated tops already emit imported package roots alongside
their embedded parent and worker modules. The old GeneratedChildRealizer
selects only the child's single AST, discarding sibling packages before
SourceFrontend collects them. An isolated imported record-input carrier
therefore refuses even though its individual module artifacts strictly replay.
The extraction starts in d008a23278f58c4875427f09a087082558f4012d; subsequent
strict-boundary work also passes the selected child AST to the frontend.

Embedded FSM and DT realization now combines the detached child root with
the composition's detached package roots. Existing strict source validation,
package import declarations and the normal resolver retain admission. This
adds no package imports or symbols to a child that does not declare them.
External child files bypass this handoff and retain their own source-relative
package lookup; a same-name top package cannot replace or fill that dependency.

T2020 uses actual strict embedded FSM/DT realization and full composition
pipelines, reused definitions, independently expected recursive record types
and packed struct member widths, missing/undeclared-package refusals and external local
package precedence. Complete composition facts and source bytes stay unchanged.
The final canonical witnesses fail against the exact committed predecessor
9aaa27bbb7c072dab52b486b64f93309e55cfa99 while external controls pass.
Early draft infix syntax, context-prefix diagnostic extraction, one-child C2
selection, bit-vector HDL syntax and resolver-message capitalization expectations are corrected oracle limits,
not product qualification. T2019 qualifies actual authored ISF carriers.

Re-derivation uses actual compiler/realizer products and literal type/wiring
expectations. Exact predecessor failures and missing/external package controls
provide distinct falsification. Tracked producers, tests, maintained source,
this fact, its owner and Git preserve durability. Native HDL execution and
complete generated/domain public closure remain separate obligations.

`build_top_input_links` excludes an explicit whole top-input endpoint before

widths and types first, then skipped the explicitly owned top input too late.
This rejected an ISF public `ready` input despite its explicit domain route,
because CDC children also expose `ready` outputs. Top-output inference already
used the earlier exclusion.

`LinkedPlanBuilder` still resolves each authored link and validates source and
target roles, width agreement, declared types and duplicate drivers. Unrouted
top inputs retain their ordinary same-name admission checks; a child-only link
does not claim an unrelated top input. Implicit ports and declared-by-name
lanes retain their existing rules. This change does not widen source-expression
ownership or invent partial-port inference semantics.

T175 exercises unrelated direction/width/interface-type/declared-type conflicts
with and without explicit ownership. T176 confirms actual link validation.

artifact checks, and complete native/API/newline MCP success/failure equality.
Its Verilog-family oracle holds the authored ready input low, verifies that
completion remains blocked, then releases it and repeats around reset. Runtime
qualification requires a real qualified Verilator provider, using the existing
Darwin qualification switch where applicable; a skip does not qualify behavior.

HDL, provider/producer identities and the test receipts.

oracle with the non-colliding `work_ready` name: `_inj_watchdog` places
initialization in the await state, then external-activation rewriting adds a

timeout and premature acknowledgement. `.32.1.3.3.3` owns repair, rearming and

transaction entry and retains the original failing source/HDL; a leading

The pre-migration legacy surface contained 37 literal `verilator --binary`
compile calls and 37 matching generated-runtime calls across 34 test files.
Thirty-six runtime calls in 33 files used `IPC::Cmd::run` without a timeout.
The remaining direct baseline in `t/1559` used a 30-second `IPC::Cmd` alarm
timeout without whole-process-group cleanup. None had a pre-discovery Darwin
guard. The owning task and closed tracked test manifest retain that exact
per-path inventory and independent compile/runtime file-set comparison.

Decision `0086` is implemented by test-only
`FSM::Test::VerilatorRuntime`. It owns version, compile, and runtime processes
at the existing qualified
10/120/30-second walls and 65,536/8,388,608/67,108,864-byte capture limits.
It uses scalar argv only, a close-on-exec handoff channel, separate bounded
stdout/stderr, monotonic timing, one process group, TERM/KILL escalation,
leader reaping, and verified group disappearance. Timeout, capture overflow,
signal, nonzero exit, handoff failure, or cleanup failure stays failed; there
is no retry. All 37 compile and 37 generated-runtime callsites in the exact
34-file set are helper-owned, and no direct generated-binary IPC launch
remains.

Standard Darwin execution of the affected surface is explicit through
`FSMGEN_DARWIN_VERILATOR_TEST_RUNTIME=1`. The caller emits its TAP skip before
tool discovery, and the helper independently refuses an unqualified Darwin
process before `fork`/`exec`. Non-Darwin execution and every existing
generated-HDL/testbench/oracle remain unchanged. The focused hostile watcher
validates the closed census manifest, independently scans the tracked tests,
rejects new unbounded direct paths, and proves overflow, timeout, surviving-
descendant, exec, signal, nonzero, guard, environment, and cleanup behavior.

Decision `0087` later extracted the unchanged process mechanics into private
`FSM::Test::ProcessSupervisor` so another bounded test domain could reuse them.
`FSM::Test::VerilatorRuntime` remains the only policy owner for this surface:
its schema, Darwin guard, stage admission, fixed bounds, path checks, and
observable behavior are unchanged. A focused watcher rejects direct low-level
use by non-policy helper modules.

This is verification-test process supervision, not IASIM execution and not a
new FSMGEN execution profile. It neither exposes nor replaces the private
`FSM::VIAL::Backend::VerilatorLifecycle`; existing VIAL public, diagnostic,
and measurement guards remain under decisions `0083`-`0085`.

The long `t/296` corpus matrix has a separate opt-in continuity contract.
Set `FSMGEN_T296_CHECKPOINT` to a safe relative
`.artifacts/t296/<safe-name>.json` path before starting it under the RAM guard.
Only green isolated batches completed after checkpointing was enabled receive
credit. The checkpoint rejects a dirty or different revision, another volume,
symlinks, malformed state, and another contract version; it is removed only
after the complete parent passes. An uncheckpointed interruption has no
reconstructable credit and must restart t296. A host-pressure interruption may
resume the exact command with the same checkpoint after headroom returns; it
does not justify raising either RAM ceiling or weakening the matrix.

External-command doubles use repository-local test temp and the canonical running interpreter, never host `true`/`false` lookup.
T313 proves exit truth beside hostile PATH traps. Decision 0101 keeps 120-second/8,388,608-byte HDL steps after T1524 measured 46,647,945 ordinary versus zero quiet Yosys bytes; quiet failure kept `ERROR:`. It selects `-q` plus head/tail excerpts retaining 65,536 tool bytes with a separate bounded marker. Split capture, exact success, timeout, cleanup/no-retry, Perl handoff, and VIAL authority stay unchanged; `.19.2.3.1.2.2.3.2` owns implementation.

Raw Lispish type forms wrap their aggregate body; the ISF adapter produces

---

Direct SystemVerilog generation now reroutes only the top state and
standalone-DT generated-enable condition block through `StructuralRTLIR`
assignment records.

The legacy direct backend emits explicit temporary markers around that block
only when the direct pipeline asks for the reroute handoff. After
`StructuralRTLIR` is built, `FSM::Backend::GeneratedModuleEmitter` replaces the
marked block with the matching top generated-enable assignment records and
removes the markers before final HDL is returned. Unmarked HDL text is not
parsed.

DT-specific WEN/EN assignments, LHS-level enables, output-drive and
always-block bodies, direct instances/links, VHDL emission, and full direct
module emission remain outside this reroute slice.

Assignment enable identity is allocated before factorization by
`FSM::Synthesis::EnableGraph::AssignmentSupport`. One fresh registry per
complete analysis build covers DT-local and LHS-level families, reserving
module signals, effective system ports, parameters and top-level state/DT
enable names. Sorted original LHS/DT/RHS
traversal and suffix probing separate case/punctuation and cross-family
collisions while preserving available readable candidates. Muxes, structural
records and emitted HDL consume the allocated identity.

The prior per-LHS registry allowed `PENABLE` and `penable` to share
`penable_0_en`; duplicate factorization context keys then replaced one original
condition with the other in hash-dependent order. T1866 guards this and related
collisions; the prior expression-alias guard remains T1405. Exact baseline,
isolated controls, actual CLI/MCP comparisons and HDL behavior evidence are in
`docs/audits/mcp-feature-coverage-20260924/enable-identity-repair.json` under
`SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.31.2.1`. This is an assignment-enable
namespace contract, not a universal generated-identifier collision claim.

Simulator qualification is distinct from enable identity. The installed Icarus
13.0 output-context probe returns a false `$onehot0` result for one-hot
concatenations while packed/literal checks and the basic truth-table control
pass. APB assertion diagnostics also depend on expression context. Do not
accept a final testbench PASS after simulator ERRORs. Assertion-enabled
Verilator 5.050 passes the bounded probe and APB transfer oracle; this is not
universal four-state or scheduling equivalence. Compiler conflict checks stay
unchanged; T1542's native Verilog Icarus lane has no SystemVerilog assertions.
Reproduction, explicit expected-value checker, negative controls and versions:
`docs/audits/mcp-feature-coverage-20260924/onehot-qualification.json` and
`docs/book/src/09-generated-hdl-debugging-and-inspection.md` (runtime simulator
qualification), owned by `SEMANTIC-INTROSPECTION-MCP-FRONTIER.31.2.6`.

Direct VHDL recognizes generated parenthesized unary OR/AND/XOR before generic
rewrites. Declared scalars and in-range static bit selects lower by identity or
complement. Declared vectors lower through backend-owned `std_logic` fold
helpers; signed vectors cast explicitly to `std_logic_vector`, and complemented
forms apply `not` to the helper result.

Only required helpers are emitted. They fold OR/XOR from `'0'` and AND from
`'1'`, preserving `std_logic` unknown propagation without using unqualified
native vector-reduction syntax. Helper-name collisions, ranges, invalid
selects, unresolved/compound/malformed operands, and residual reduction tokens
fail closed before output.

The real named-drive positive and complemented scalar reductions are now
token-free. Existing AMBA `HRESP` and APB `wait_ctr`/`addr_q` vector truthiness
remains supported through the helpers. Public one-operand source forms remain
rejected, and decision `0023` still withholds external VHDL compile/runtime
qualification because no authoritative compiler is installed.

skipped T1542 is not executable evidence. Retain the RAM guard defaults.

native vector syntax or claim executable VHDL qualification.

Before `DIRECT-VHDL-REDUCTION-EXPRESSION-LOWERING.2`, the direct VHDL scaffold
accepted a scheduled named-drive FSM but emitted
`drive_zero_en and (|drive_zero_start)`. The prefix `|` was a SystemVerilog
unary reduction token, not valid VHDL expression syntax.

Root cause is `_sv_expr_to_vhdl`: it translates spaced binary `|` to `or` but
has no unary reduction-expression translation or fail-closed guard. The same
probe generates SystemVerilog and Verilog; Icarus 13.0 compiles the Verilog.
No `ghdl`, `nvc`, or `vcom` is installed, and the repository's external VHDL
validation lane remains deferred.

Generation success is therefore not VHDL qualification for this shape. Parent
selector `.831` chose the independent
`DIRECT-VHDL-REDUCTION-EXPRESSION-LOWERING` audit and repair; clean selector
commit `5f904d2d2` activated the no-behavior audit before the later repair.

Completed audit `.1` proves the original named-drive operand is declared
scalar and selects proposed `.2`: positive scalar unary OR/AND/XOR becomes
identity and complemented scalar reduction becomes VHDL `not`. Implementation
preservation proved blanket vector rejection would regress AMBA/APB paths, so
completed `.2` instead emits required-only `std_logic` vector folds while
keeping ranges/unresolved/compound forms fail-closed. t1542/t1543 now prove the
named-drive output is token-free. No external VHDL compiler claim is implied.

Runtime revalidation on Darwin requires the separately qualified opt-in; a
skipped T1542 is not executable evidence. Retain the RAM guard defaults.

Any downstream-visible change must keep the codebase, downstream
handoff/integration docs, public contracts, capability-manifest metadata,
support-accounting catalog entries, tests, explicit deferrals, and mdBook in
lockstep. These surfaces convey the same facts from different viewpoints for
any downstream consumer; drift is a project bug.

The doctrine is generic to all downstream consumers. SPECFORGE is one consumer,
but the integration handoff, public contracts, capability manifest, support
accounting, and mdBook are not SPECFORGE-specific.

For `.isf` and `.ppif`, the lockstep surfaces include

semantic JSON were identical after normalizing only documented revision/path

code, docs, and tests agree, and the CI repair did not change it. That old

proposed tree `DOWNSTREAM-SOURCE-PROVENANCE-CONTRACT`; its `.1` leaf must select

that chapter. The landing page remains the GitHub index and keeps its
repository-relative part links.

future classification for the shipped AXI/APB/AHB suffixes. Downstream section
8 now gives a complete lowering-clean input/storage/output record example and
exact copy, field/sample, physical writer, domain and target-profile boundaries.

SystemVerilog observations and remaining output generated/field/runtime gates

Actual example native/API/newline, strict carriers, literal metadata and current

date: 2026-09-30
